l1: What Windows version is the affected system running? (Get-ComputerInfo | Select OsName,OsVersion,OsBuildNumber)
Is this a Windows client (Windows 10/11) or Windows Server? Windows Firewall with Advanced Security is available on both editions.
Are you troubleshooting inbound traffic being blocked, outbound traffic being blocked, or application connectivity issues?
Is the system domain-joined, workgroup, or Azure AD joined? Domain profile rules apply differently.
Is the issue affecting a single computer or multiple computers in the environment?
Are third-party firewalls or security agents installed alongside Windows Firewall? (Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Where Name -like '*firewall*')
l2: Which firewall profile is active on the affected network adapter? (Get-NetFirewallProfile | Select Name,Enabled,DefaultInboundAction,DefaultOutboundAction)
Are inbound connections blocked by default policy or specific firewall rules? (Get-NetFirewallRule | Where Direction -eq Inbound | Select Name,Enabled,Action,Profile)
Are outbound connections blocked by default policy or specific firewall rules? (Get-NetFirewallRule | Where Direction -eq Outbound | Select Name,Enabled,Action,Profile)
Is the Windows Firewall service running? (Get-Service MpsSvc | Select Status,StartType)
Are there conflicting rules that might be interfering? (Get-NetFirewallRule | Sort Priority -Descending | Select Name,Priority,Action -First 20)
Is Windows Defender Firewall Control integrated with other security components like Windows Defender ATP or Endpoint Protection?
Are you troubleshooting remote desktop (RDP), file sharing (SMB), or specific application traffic?
Is IPSec/Connection Security rules configured and causing the issue? (Get-NetIPSecRule | Select Name,Enabled,Mode,Profile)
Are network isolation or container-specific firewall rules involved?
Is the system behind a perimeter firewall or using VPN which might affect rule requirements?

l1: Check Windows Firewall service status: 'Get-Service MpsSvc' — should be Running with Automatic or Automatic (Delayed Start) startup type.
Check active firewall profiles: 'Get-NetFirewallProfile' — verify Domain, Private, Public profiles are correctly enabled with expected default actions.
List enabled inbound rules: 'Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Enabled True | Select Name,Action,Profile' — identify rules blocking traffic.
List enabled outbound rules: 'Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Outbound -Enabled True | Select Name,Action,Profile' — identify outbound restrictions.
Test connectivity with firewall enabled: 'Test-NetConnection -ComputerName <target> -Port <port>' — if fails, firewall may be blocking.
Check firewall event logs: 'Get-WinEvent -LogName "Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security/Firewall" -MaxEvents 20' — look for blocked connection events.
l2: Export complete firewall rule set: 'Get-NetFirewallRule | Export-Csv C:\firewall_rules.csv -NoTypeInformation' — review for unexpected rules.
Check IPSec main mode rules: 'Get-NetIPSecMainModeRule | Select Name,Enabled,Profile' — verify IPSec policy configuration.
Check IPSec quick mode rules: 'Get-NetIPSecQuickModeRule | Select Name,Enabled,Profile' — verify IPSec phase 2 configuration.
Check connection security rules: 'Get-NetIPSecRule | Select Name,Enabled,Profile,Mode' — verify authentication and encryption requirements.
Check firewall state for specific application: 'Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter | Select Program' — identify applications with specific rules.
Check firewall state for specific service: 'Get-NetFirewallServiceFilter | Select Service' — identify services with specific rules.
Check firewall state for specific port: 'Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Select LocalPort,Protocol' — identify port-specific rules.
Check firewall state for specific address: 'Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter | Select RemoteAddress,LocalAddress' — identify address-specific rules.
Check network adapter profiles: 'Get-NetConnectionProfile | Select Name,NetworkCategory,IPv4Connectivity' — verify adapter profile assignments.
Test with firewall temporarily disabled (not recommended in production): 'Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Private,Public -Enabled False' — retest connectivity, then re-enable immediately.

Capture firewall ETL trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security tracefile=C:\firewall_trace.etl' — reproduce issue, then 'netsh trace stop'.

l1: If Windows Firewall service is not running: Start it with 'Start-Service MpsSvc' — if it fails, check dependencies (Base Filtering Engine, IKE and AuthIP IPsec Keying Modules).

If inbound traffic is blocked: Create an allow rule for the specific port: 'New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Allow <port>" -Direction Inbound -LocalPort <port> -Protocol TCP -Action Allow -Profile Domain,Private,Public'.

If outbound traffic is blocked: Create an allow rule for the specific application: 'New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "Allow <app>" -Direction Outbound -Program "<path>" -Action Allow -Profile Domain,Private,Public'.
If network profile is incorrect: Change adapter profile with 'Set-NetConnectionProfile -Name <adapter> -NetworkCategory Private' — Domain profile requires domain authentication.
If rules are missing: Restore default firewall rules with 'netsh advfirewall reset' — this restores Windows defaults but removes custom rules.
If third-party firewall conflicts: Disable third-party firewall temporarily to isolate — if Windows Firewall works after disabling, third-party is the issue.
l2: If rule priority is causing issues: Adjust rule priority with 'Set-NetFirewallRule -Name <rule> -Priority <value>' — lower numeric value = higher priority (1-65535).
If IPSec authentication fails: Verify IKE and AuthIP service is running: 'Get-Service IKEEXT' — check computer certificates for EAP-TLS or Kerberos authentication.
If outbound default action is Block: Change to Allow with 'Set-NetFirewallProfile -Profile Domain,Private,Public -DefaultOutboundAction Allow' — use with caution, only for troubleshooting.
If rule scope is too restrictive: Modify address filters with 'Set-NetFirewallRule -Name <rule> -RemoteAddress Any' — or specify specific subnet ranges.
If application is blocked but should be allowed: Verify rule is using correct program path: 'Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter -AssociatedNetFirewallRule <rule>' — update if path changed.

If GPO is pushing conflicting rules: Check applied GPO with 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html' — review Computer Configuration > Windows Settings > Security Settings > Windows Firewall with Advanced Security.
If container firewall is blocking: Check Docker or Windows Container firewall rules with 'Get-NetFirewallHyperVRule' or 'Get-NetFirewallHyperVVMSetting'.
If rule exists but not applied: Verify rule is enabled and matches active profile: 'Get-NetFirewallRule -Name <rule> | Select Enabled,Profile' — enable if disabled, add profile if missing.
If network location detection is wrong: Force network location with 'Set-NetConnectionProfile -NetworkCategory Private' — or use Group Policy to control network location.
If firewall blocking during boot: Check boot-time rules with 'Get-NetFirewallBoottimeRule' — these rules apply before firewall service starts.

l1: Export all firewall rules: 'Get-NetFirewallRule | Export-Csv C:\firewall_rules.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export firewall profiles: 'Get-NetFirewallProfile | Export-Csv C:\firewall_profiles.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export firewall event logs: 'wevtutil epl "Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security/Firewall" C:\firewall_events.evtx'
Export network connection profiles: 'Get-NetConnectionProfile | Export-Csv C:\connection_profiles.csv -NoTypeInformation'
l2: Export IPSec rules: 'Get-NetIPSecRule | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_rules.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export IPSec main mode rules: 'Get-NetIPSecMainModeRule | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_mainmode.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export IPSec quick mode rules: 'Get-NetIPSecQuickModeRule | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_quickmode.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export firewall application filters: 'Get-NetFirewallApplicationFilter | Export-Csv C:\firewall_app_filters.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export firewall service filters: 'Get-NetFirewallServiceFilter | Export-Csv C:\firewall_service_filters.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export firewall port filters: 'Get-NetFirewallPortFilter | Export-Csv C:\firewall_port_filters.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export firewall address filters: 'Get-NetFirewallAddressFilter | Export-Csv C:\firewall_address_filters.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export IPSec main mode SA: 'Get-NetIPsecMainModeSA | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_mainmode_sa.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export IPSec quick mode SA: 'Get-NetIPsecQuickModeSA | Export-Csv C:\ipsec_quickmode_sa.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Export network adapter settings: 'Get-NetAdapter | Export-Csv C:\network_adapters.csv -NoTypeInformation'
Generate GPO report: 'gpresult /h C:\gpo_report.html' — review firewall-related GPO settings.

Capture firewall ETL trace: 'netsh trace start capture=yes provider=Microsoft-Windows-Windows Firewall With Advanced Security level=5 tracefile=C:\firewall_trace.etl' — reproduce issue — 'netsh trace stop'.
Export System event log: 'wevtutil epl System C:\system_events.evtx' — contains firewall service events.
Export Application event log: 'wevtutil epl Application C:\app_events.evtx' — contains application firewall events.
TSS data collection: '.\TSS.ps1 -Scenario NET_General' — collects comprehensive network diagnostics including firewall state.

inbound_blocked.title: Inbound traffic blocked by Windows Firewall

steps.expect: Status: Running, StartType: Automatic or Automatic (Delayed Start)
Profiles are enabled — DefaultInboundAction: Block is normal for security
TcpTestSucceeded: False if firewall is blocking

steps.action: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Inbound -Enabled True | Where Action -eq Block | Select Name,LocalPort,Profile
steps.expect: Identify specific block rules for the target port
Verify active network profile matches rule profile scope
Look for Event ID 2004-2006 indicating blocked connections
Rule created successfully
Rule enabled if not already enabled
TcpTestSucceeded: True — connectivity restored
Enabled: True, Action: Allow

outbound_blocked.title: Outbound traffic blocked by Windows Firewall

steps.expect: DefaultOutboundAction: Block indicates outbound blocking is enabled
TcpTestSucceeded: False if outbound traffic is blocked

steps.action: Get-NetFirewallRule -Direction Outbound -Enabled True | Where Action -eq Block | Select Name,Program,Profile
steps.expect: Identify specific outbound block rules
Verify application path matches the blocked application
Rule created successfully
Default outbound action changed to Allow — use with caution
TcpTestSucceeded: True — outbound connectivity restored
Status: Running — IKE and AuthIP service must be operational
Verify IPSec rules are enabled and match active profile
Check for failed or non-existent main mode SAs
Look for IPSec authentication failure events
Verify computer certificates exist for EAP-TLS authentication
IKE and AuthIP service started if stopped
Windows Firewall service restarted to apply IPSec changes
IPSec rule enabled if disabled
Main mode SA established with target
